Use this while turning a question into a search strategy. Start with the core concepts and the terms used by relevant sources, then translate them into each database's vocabulary.


<details class="template-copy">
<summary>Open the blank copyable template</summary>

Copy this plain-text version into your approved project record. Repeat entry fields as needed and remove prompts that do not apply. The guidance and examples below help you complete it.

```text
Search-concept table

Blank table

Concept: [ ]
Natural-language terms: [ ]
Variants and abbreviations: [ ]
Controlled vocabulary: [database heading]
Related or contrary terms: [ ]
Source and rationale: [seed/source]

Elements not searched and why: [ ]
Known relevant records used to test retrieval: [ ]
Version/date: [ ]
```

</details>

## Completed example

*Illustrative example; replace these details with your own verified record.*

| Concept | Natural-language terms | Variants and abbreviations | Controlled vocabulary | Related or contrary terms | Source and rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| doctoral participation | engagement; participation | PhD; doctoral; postgraduate research | database-specific | withdrawal; persistence; isolation | recent review and student terminology |

**Not searched:** wellbeing outcome, because it is inconsistently indexed and will be assessed during screening.

## Check your record

Test the draft against known relevant records and investigate misses. A list of synonyms is preparation for a search, not evidence that the topic has been covered.

## Scenario test

A known relevant paper uses “withdrawal” rather than “disengagement”. The contrary-term column exposes the omission before the full search.
